title: Macroeconomics Adventure 1: AD–AS and the Multiplier
welcome_lead: Today you'll model output with AD = C+I+G+(X−M) and amplify it with the multiplier.
meta_desc: Economics Macro: aggregate demand and supply, equilibrium output and the Keynesian multiplier.
final_note: You built AD and SRAS curves and computed multiplier effects on national income.

concepts.def: C + I + G + (X − M) at each price level
Difference of actual vs potential GDP

walkthroughs.body_html:
AD = C + I + G + (X − M).

Consumption — biggest share, driven by income, wealth, confidence, interest rates.
Investment — firm capital, driven by interest rates and 'animal spirits'.
Government spending — fiscal policy lever.
(X − M) net exports — driven by foreign income and exchange rates.

walkthroughs.h2: AS in short and long run
walkthroughs.body_html:
SRAS slopes up — firms produce more at higher prices when wages and other inputs lag.

LRAS is vertical at potential output (Yf) — in the classical view economies return to full employment.

Keynesian LRAS has a horizontal section at low output and a vertical section at Yf.

Keynes (1936): an injection circulates through the economy.

k = 1 / (1 − MPC) = 1 / MPW where MPW = MPS + MPT + MPM.

If MPC = 0.8, k = 5. A $10bn injection raises GDP by $50bn — subject to spare capacity.
